title: How to build an invoice tracker (columns, rules) | 50agents
description: Build an invoice tracker with eight columns, five statuses and two formulas, days late and amount still due, then a Late view and a weekly check.
h1: How to build an invoice tracker
answer: Keep one row per invoice with eight columns, five statuses, and a Late view of unpaid invoices past due, oldest first.
Mark Paid the day money arrives, and it tells you who owes you and since when.

body.p: In a QuickBooks survey of US small businesses, more than half were owed money on unpaid invoices. Most of it is not refusal; it is invoices nobody followed up. Track invoices you send here, and keep bills you pay in a separate list.

head: Column
Example
Note
rows: The accounts address, not your contact
Add currency if you bill in several
Due is sent date plus terms
Draft, Sent, Reminded, Paid, Written off

method.h2: How to build an invoice tracker, step by step

steps.title: Create the list
steps.body: The columns above, in a sheet or a no-code app. Make Status a dropdown.

steps.title: Bring in every open invoice
steps.body: Export from your invoicing or accounting app as CSV, or type them in. Open ones first; paid history can wait.

steps.title: Add a Late view
steps.body: Filter: status not Paid or Written off, due date before today. Sort by due date, oldest first.

note.text: In a sheet, a Days late column does this: =IF(AND(G2<>"Paid",F2<TODAY()),TODAY()-F2,"").

steps.title: Add three totals
steps.body: Still to collect (everything Sent or Reminded), Late, and Paid this month. Three numbers you can read in a second.

steps.title: Update it the day money lands
steps.body: Check the bank or payment app and mark Paid.

note.text: A tracker a week behind the bank sends you chasing clients who already paid.

steps.title: Decide what happens to late ones
steps.body: Set a reminder schedule: see [how to automate invoice reminders](/guides/how-to-automate-invoice-reminders).

captain.line: Captain builds this tracker as an app, with To collect, Late and All invoices views, the three totals, and an AI agent that drafts a reminder for your yes.

wrong.title: Part payments marked Paid
wrong.body: Half arrives, the row turns green, and the rest is forgotten. Add a Part paid status and the amount still due.

wrong.title: Duplicate invoice numbers
wrong.body: Two invoices called INV-1049 after a template copy. Make the number unique and check before adding.

wrong.title: Receivables and bills in one list
wrong.body: Money in and money out get mixed up. Keep two trackers.

wrong.title: Due dates from the wrong terms
wrong.body: Net 30 for a client on Net 14. Store terms per client and compute the due date from them.

faqs.q: What should an invoice tracker include?
faqs.a: Invoice number, client, billing email, amount, sent date, due date, status and notes. Add currency and amount paid if you need them.

faqs.q: How do I track unpaid invoices in Excel or Google Sheets?
faqs.a: One row per invoice with a Status dropdown, a Days late formula, and a filter view of everything not Paid with a due date before today, sorted oldest first.

faqs.q: Should I use my accounting app instead?
faqs.a: If every invoice is raised there, yes: it already tracks payments. A separate tracker earns its place when invoices come from several places or you want reminders drafted for you.
